title: A Case That Could Transform America’s Relationship With Guns

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk,
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、

sentences.en: Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、Zylran Mondani以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.en: We're going to be live streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日通过nytimes.com进行部分采访的直播，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今日要闻。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court heard arguments in the first major gun case in more than a decade.
sentences.zh: 最高法院审理了十多年来第一起重大的枪支案件。

sentences.en: I talked to my colleague, Adam Liptak, about how the justices might rule and what that will mean for guns in America.
sentences.zh: 我与同事亚当·利普塔克讨论了大法官们可能如何裁决，以及这对美国的枪支问题意味着什么。

sentences.en: Plus, the trillion-dollar infrastructure bill has finally passed.
sentences.zh: 此外，万亿美元的基础设施法案终于通过了。

sentences.en: It's Monday, November 8th.
sentences.zh: 今天是11月8日，星期一。

sentences.en: Adam, it's nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 亚当，很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: And you.
sentences.zh: 我也是。

sentences.en: So, Adam, tell me what the basic facts are of this case.
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，请告诉我这个案件的基本事实。

sentences.en: So, two men in upstate New York wanted to get licenses to carry handguns most anywhere.
sentences.zh: 纽约州北部的两名男子想要获得在几乎任何地方携带手枪的许可证。

sentences.en: Robert
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·

sentences.en: Nash and Brandon Koch applied for a license.
sentences.zh: 纳什和布兰登·科赫申请了许可证。

sentences.en: And they were told, yes, you can have licenses to do target practice and go hunting.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知，是的，你们可以获得用于打靶练习和狩猎的许可证。

sentences.en: And one of them was allowed to carry a gun to and from work.
sentences.zh: 其中一人被允许在往返工作地点时携带枪支。

sentences.en: But they were denied the right to have a handgun anywhere.
sentences.zh: 但他们被拒绝了在任何地方携带手枪的权利。

sentences.en: And they sued.
sentences.zh: 于是他们提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: And they said that violated the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 他们声称这违反了宪法第二修正案。

sentences.en: Why were they denied?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么被拒绝？

sentences.en: How does the law actually work in New York?
sentences.zh: 纽约的法律实际上是如何运作的？

sentences.en: New York, like about seven states, requires you to demonstrate a proper cause to carry a gun.
sentences.zh: 纽约州和大约七个州一样，要求你证明有正当理由才能携带枪支。

sentences.en: What does proper cause mean?
sentences.zh: 什么是正当理由？

sentences.en: Well, that's an open question.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: Proper cause means you have a better reason than the average citizen.
sentences.zh: 正当理由意味着你有一个比普通公民更好的理由。

sentences.en: Maybe you work in the Diamond District and you're carrying goods back and forth.
sentences.zh: 也许你在钻石区工作，需要来回运送货物。

sentences.en: But if you just want a gun as a general matter for self-defense, for no particular threat, but in a dangerous world, New York will generally turn you down.
sentences.zh: 但如果你只是想为了自卫而拥有一把枪，并没有特定的威胁，只是因为世界很危险，纽约通常会拒绝你。

sentences.en: New York will say, no, you don't have a good enough reason.
sentences.zh: 纽约会说，不，你没有足够好的理由。

sentences.en: You don't have a special reason.
sentences.zh: 你没有特殊的理由。

sentences.en: You don't have an atypical reason.
sentences.zh: 你没有非典型的理由。

sentences.en: And that system of licensing guns for public carry is not unusual.
sentences.zh: 而这种公共场所携带枪支的许可制度并不罕见。

sentences.en: California has it, Hawaii, Maryland,
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚州、夏威夷州、马里兰州、

sentences.en: Massachusetts, New Jersey, Rhode Island, about a quarter of the population of the U.S.
sentences.zh: 马萨诸塞州、新泽西州、罗德岛州都有这种制度，覆盖了美国约四分之一的人口。

sentences.en: And of course, some of these places have big, big urban areas.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中一些地方拥有非常庞大的城市区域。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So they're denied this license to carry a concealed weapon anywhere because they haven't shown that they have this special need.
sentences.zh: 所以他们被拒绝了在任何地方携带隐蔽武器的许可证，因为他们没有证明自己有这种特殊需求。

sentences.en: Where does the case go next?
sentences.zh: 这个案件接下来会怎样？

sentences.en: In the lower federal courts, they lose.
sentences.zh: 在联邦下级法院，他们败诉了。

sentences.en: The lower federal courts say New York is entitled to regulate guns.
sentences.zh: 联邦下级法院认为纽约有权监管枪支。

sentences.en: The guns are dangerous in themselves.
sentences.zh: 枪支本身就是危险的。

sentences.en: And there's good reason to think you shouldn't let anyone anywhere have a gun, even for the stated purpose of self-defense.
sentences.zh: 而且有充分的理由认为，即使是为了自卫，也不应该让任何人随处携带枪支。

sentences.en: And it goes to the Supreme
sentences.zh: 案件随后上诉到了最高

sentences.en: Court, which had, in 2008, kind of revolutionized Second Amendment law in a case called District of Columbia against Teller, which did one big thing and one small thing.
sentences.zh: 法院。最高法院在2008年通过“哥伦比亚特区诉海勒案”彻底改变了第二修正案的法律，该案做了一件大事和一件小事。

sentences.en: The big thing that it did was maybe partly symbolic, was it said people have an individual right to own guns untied to militia service.
sentences.zh: 它所做的大事，或许在某种程度上具有象征意义，即它宣布人们拥有与民兵服役无关的个人拥有枪支的权利。

sentences.en: Let me read you the text of the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 让我为你读一下第二修正案的文本。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: It says, a well-regulated militia being necessary to the security of a free state, the right of the people to keep and bear arms shall not be infringed.
sentences.zh: 它写道：纪律严明的民兵是保障自由州的安全所必需的，人民持有和携带武器的权利不得侵犯。

sentences.en: And for the longest time, people thought that that first clause, the militia clause, told you what the amendment was about.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，人们认为第一条款，即民兵条款，说明了修正案的宗旨。

sentences.en: You know, you have a right to keep and bear arms in connection with service in a state militia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你拥有与在州民兵组织服役相关的持有和携带武器的权利。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And the structure of the sentence can easily be read that way.
sentences.zh: 这个句子的结构很容易被那样解读。

sentences.en: But the Supreme Court in 2008 said, no, that's not the right way to read it.
sentences.zh: 但最高法院在2008年表示，不，那不是正确的解读方式。

sentences.en: The introductory phrase is illustrative of one reason you might have a right to keep and bear arMs. But a reason, perhaps the main reason, is for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 导言部分说明了你可能拥有持有和携带武器权利的一个原因。但另一个原因，或许是主要原因，是为了自卫。

sentences.en: So that's a big change in the understanding of the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: 所以这对第二修正案的理解是一个巨大的改变。

sentences.en: At the same time, it did only a small thing.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，它只做了一件小事。

sentences.en: It applied that principle that you have an individual right to keep and bear arms to the home.
sentences.zh: 它将你拥有持有和携带武器的个人权利这一原则应用到了家庭领域。

sentences.en: And it said that a DC law that made it all but impossible to have a handgun in the home for self-defense was no good.
sentences.zh: 它裁定哥伦比亚特区一项几乎禁止在家里拥有自卫手枪的法律是无效的。

sentences.en: And that's essentially everything the
sentences.zh: 而这基本上就是迄今为止

sentences.en: Supreme Court has told us to date about the scope of Second Amendment rights.
sentences.zh: 最高法院告诉我们关于第二修正案权利范围的全部内容。

sentences.en: So this new case, which leaves the home and asks the question of what's the scope of the Second Amendment outside the home, is an enormous question.
sentences.zh: 所以这个新案件离开了家庭领域，提出了第二修正案在家庭之外的范围是什么的问题，这是一个巨大的问题。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Adam, let me make sure I understand.
sentences.zh: 那么亚当，让我确认我理解得对不对。

sentences.en: So Heller essentially says that the Second Amendment gives any individual the right to have arms as self-defense in the home.
sentences.zh: 海勒案本质上说，第二修正案赋予任何个人在家里自卫时拥有武器的权利。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be connected with a militia.
sentences.zh: 它不必与民兵组织挂钩。

sentences.en: They have that right, period, whether they're part of a militia or not.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有这种权利，句号，无论他们是否是民兵组织的一员。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But it was narrow in the sense that it was only talking about guns in homes.
sentences.zh: 但它很狭隘，因为它只讨论了家里的枪支。

sentences.en: It didn't go outside the door of the home at all.
sentences.zh: 它根本没有走出家门。

sentences.en: So the whole question of what you can do and how states can regulate outside the home is completely unsolved law.
sentences.zh: 所以关于你在外面能做什么以及各州如何监管的问题，在法律上完全没有定论。

sentences.en: It's open field, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这是一片空白领域，是的。

sentences.en: And the lower courts have disagreed about what the Second Amendment has to say about guns outside the home.
sentences.zh: 下级法院对于第二修正案在家庭之外对枪支的规定存在分歧。

sentences.en: So this new case with these two guys in upstate New York is about whether you can have a concealed weapon as a right to self-defense outside the home.
sentences.zh: 所以这个涉及纽约州北部两名男子的新案件，是关于你是否拥有作为自卫权利在家庭之外携带隐蔽武器的权利。

sentences.en: That feels huge.
sentences.zh: 这感觉意义重大。

sentences.en: Oh, it's big.
sentences.zh: 哦，这非常重大。

sentences.en: This case, but for a couple of, I guess, maybe even bigger abortion cases this term, would be a blockbuster in any term.
sentences.zh: 如果不是因为本届最高法院还有几起可能更重大的堕胎案件，这起案件在任何一届任期内都会是重磅炸弹。

sentences.en: And the consequences will be huge.
sentences.zh: 其后果将是巨大的。

sentences.en: It will affect a quarter of the population of the United States.
sentences.zh: 它将影响美国四分之一的人口。

sentences.en: And it will represent the court's return to an area where it's really been silent for over a decade.
sentences.zh: 它将代表最高法院重返一个十多年来一直保持沉默的领域。

sentences.en: And also bear in mind that we now have a supercharged six to three conservative majority.
sentences.zh: 还要记住，我们现在有一个六比三的强力保守派多数派。

sentences.en: And what the court does here may well transform the relationship between Americans and guns.
sentences.zh: 法院在这里所做的裁决很可能会改变美国人与枪支之间的关系。

sentences.en: So I was particularly interested in the oral argument in the case to get a sense of where, after all these years, the justices were going on this issue.
sentences.zh: 所以我对该案的口头辩论特别感兴趣，想了解在这么多年后，大法官们在这个问题上的立场。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《纽约时报》才能获取所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息，去探索《纽约时报》呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《纽约时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载应用程序，获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: So, Adam, last week when the justices heard arguments on this really high-stakes gun case, how does it start?
sentences.zh: 那么，亚当，上周大法官们听取了这起高风险枪支案件的辩论，它是如何开始的？

sentences.en: The Honorable, the Chief Justice, and the Associate Justices of the Supreme Court of the United States.
sentences.zh: 尊敬的首席大法官及美国最高法院的各位大法官。

sentences.en: So, the justices come in, or eight of them do.
sentences.zh: 大法官们进场了，或者说八位大法官进场了。

sentences.en: Justice Gorsuch is participating remotely this morning.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇大法官今天上午远程参与。

sentences.en: Justice Gorsuch is home with a stomach bug, and he is participating remotely.
sentences.zh: 戈萨奇大法官因肠胃不适在家，他正在远程参与。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: We will hear argument this morning in case 2843, New York State Rifle and Pistol Association versus Bruin.
sentences.zh: 我们今天上午将审理2843号案件，纽约州步枪与手枪协会诉布鲁恩案。

sentences.en: The case promptly gets underway.
sentences.zh: 案件随即开始审理。

sentences.en: Mr. Clement?
sentences.zh: 克莱门特先生？

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，请允许我陈述。

sentences.en: Paul Clement, who represents the people seeking gun licenses from upstate New York, gets up.
sentences.zh: 代表纽约州北部寻求枪支许可的人士的保罗·克莱门特站了起来。

sentences.en: He's a very accomplished advocate.
sentences.zh: 他是一位非常有成就的辩护律师。

sentences.en: He's a former United States Solicitor General.
sentences.zh: 他曾担任美国副总检察长。

sentences.en: And he makes this basic point.
sentences.zh: 他提出了这个基本观点。

sentences.en: The text of the Second Amendment enshrines a right not just to keep arms, but to bear them.
sentences.zh: 第二修正案的文本不仅赋予了持有武器的权利，还赋予了携带武器的权利。

sentences.en: And the relevant history and tradition, exhaustively surveyed by this court in the Heller decision,
sentences.zh: 最高法院在海勒案中详尽调查的相关历史和传统，

sentences.en: confirm that the text protects an individual right to carry firearms outside the home for purposes of self-defense.
sentences.zh: 证实了该文本保护个人在家庭之外为了自卫目的携带枪支的权利。

sentences.en: He says the Second Amendment guarantees a right in the Bill of Rights, like the First Amendment, like the Fourth Amendment.
sentences.zh: 他说第二修正案保障了权利法案中的一项权利，就像第一修正案、第四修正案一样。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: It is not some extraordinary action that requires an extraordinary demonstration of need.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么需要特殊证明需求的非凡行为。

sentences.en: You shouldn't have to ask the government for permission to exercise a right.
sentences.zh: 你不应该为了行使一项权利而向政府请求许可。

sentences.en: It is the difference between regulating constitutionally protected activity and attempting to convert a fundamental constitutional right into a privilege.
sentences.zh: 这就是监管受宪法保护的活动与试图将一项基本的宪法权利转化为特权之间的区别。

sentences.en: That would turn it into a privilege, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，那会把它变成一种特权。

sentences.en: If the Second Amendment right is a real right, it can't be that most people in New York are not
sentences.zh: 如果第二修正案的权利是一项真正的权利，那么纽约的大多数人就不可能

sentences.en: allowed to exercise it and have to go to a government body to try to come up with some justification for exercising what he says is a right in the Bill of Rights.
sentences.zh: 不被允许行使它，并且必须去政府机构试图为行使他所说的权利法案中的权利寻找某种正当理由。

sentences.en: That is not how constitutional rights work.
sentences.zh: 宪法权利不是这样运作的。

sentences.en: So essentially he's saying, look, it's settled law that having a gun is a right.
sentences.zh: 所以他本质上是在说，看，拥有枪支是一项权利，这是既定法律。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But in New York, by making it so hard to actually get a license, by essentially forcing the person to prove that they need it, that's not really a right anymore.
sentences.zh: 但在纽约，通过让获得许可证变得如此困难，通过本质上强迫个人证明他们需要它，这不再是一项真正的权利了。

sentences.en: That has effectively turned it into a privilege.
sentences.zh: 这实际上已经把它变成了一种特权。

sentences.en: And that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 这是错误的。

sentences.en: Yes, that's quite right.
sentences.zh: 是的，说得非常对。

sentences.en: One way to think about it is, if this is a right like the First Amendment right to free speech or the First Amendment right to free exercise of religion, those are not rights
sentences.zh: 思考这个问题的一种方式是，如果这是一项像第一修正案赋予的言论自由或宗教自由那样的权利，那么这些权利

sentences.en: that require you to go to a government body and say, I have a good reason.
sentences.zh: 并不要求你必须去政府机构说，我有一个很好的理由。

sentences.en: I need to exercise this right.
sentences.zh: 我需要行使这项权利。

sentences.en: And it's different and better than the other guy's reason.
sentences.zh: 而且它比别人的理由更好。

sentences.en: We would all agree, I think, that those rights are just rights you possess and you don't need someone's permission to exercise them.
sentences.zh: 我想我们都会同意，这些权利只是你拥有的权利，你不需要别人的许可就能行使它们。

sentences.en: So if Clement is right, but this is a big if, that the Second Amendment right applies to carrying guns outside the home, the rest of his argument follows neatly from that.
sentences.zh: 所以如果克莱门特是对的——但这有一个很大的假设——即第二修正案的权利适用于在家庭之外携带枪支，那么他的其余论点就能顺理成章地推导出来。

sentences.en: OK, so how do the justices respond to Clement's argument?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么大法官们是如何回应克莱门特的论点的？

sentences.en: Is it supposed to say you can carry a concealed gun around the streets of the town or outside just for fun?
sentences.zh: 难道它应该说你可以为了好玩而在城镇街道上或外面携带隐蔽枪支吗？

sentences.en: I mean, they are dangerous guns.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它们是危险的枪支。

sentences.en: I mean, so what's it supposed to say?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那它应该怎么说？

sentences.en: Well, some of the more liberal justices like Justice Stephen Breyer are confused.
sentences.zh: 嗯，一些比较自由派的大法官，比如斯蒂芬·布雷耶大法官感到困惑。

sentences.en: Is we're asking that the regime work the same way for self-defense as it does for hunting.
sentences.zh: 我们是否要求该制度在自卫方面与狩猎方面以同样的方式运作？

sentences.en: I don't have to say I have a better reason to go hunting than anybody else in my general community.
sentences.zh: 我不必说我比社区里的任何人都有更好的理由去狩猎。

sentences.en: Well, the difference, of course, you have a concealed weapon to go hunting.
sentences.zh: 嗯，区别当然在于，你去狩猎时携带的是隐蔽武器。

sentences.en: You're out with an intent to shoot, say, a deer or a rabbit.
sentences.zh: 你出去的目的是射击，比如鹿或兔子。

sentences.en: But here, when you have a self-defense just for whatever you want to carry a concealed weapon, you go shooting it around and somebody gets killed.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，当你为了自卫而携带隐蔽武器时，无论你想做什么，你到处开枪，有人就会被杀。

sentences.en: And can't really quite get why it should be that, as a general matter in New York, anyone can have a gun anywhere.
sentences.zh: 真的不太明白为什么在纽约，作为一般原则，任何人都可以随处携带枪支。

sentences.en: Mr. Clement, in your opening, you talked about the right applying in any location typically open to the general public.
sentences.zh: 克莱门特先生，在你的开场白中，你谈到了这项权利适用于任何通常对公众开放的场所。

sentences.en: Other justices, the more conservative justices, seem quite persuaded by Clement's general point.
sentences.zh: 其他大法官，即那些更保守的大法官，似乎被克莱门特的总体观点说服了。

sentences.en: I'd like to get some sense about what you believe could be off limits.
sentences.zh: 我想了解一下，你认为哪些地方可以被列为禁区。

sentences.en: But they wonder whether there's not something that could be done to make sure we don't have guns everywhere.
sentences.zh: 但他们想知道，是否可以采取一些措施，确保我们不会随处可见枪支。

sentences.en: And they draw on a passage in the Heller decision which says you can regulate guns, you can bar guns from sensitive places.
sentences.zh: 他们引用了“海勒案”判决中的一段话，称你可以监管枪支，可以禁止在敏感场所携带枪支。

sentences.en: If it's a place like a courthouse, for example, a government building where everybody has to go through a magnetometer, that would qualify as a sensitive place.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果是一个法院，或者每个人都必须通过磁力计检查的政府大楼，那就可以被视为敏感场所。

sentences.en: Like schools and government buildings.
sentences.zh: 比如学校和政府大楼。

sentences.en: But the justices now have all kinds of ideas about where else you might be able to bar guns.
sentences.zh: 但大法官们现在对其他哪些地方可以禁枪有各种各样的想法。

sentences.en: New York City subways.
sentences.zh: 纽约市的地铁。

sentences.en: The subway.
sentences.zh: 地铁。

sentences.en: University campuses.
sentences.zh: 大学校园。

sentences.en: College campuses.
sentences.zh: 高校校园。

sentences.en: Time Square on New Year's Eve is a sensitive place.
sentences.zh: 除夕夜的时代广场就是一个敏感场所。

sentences.en: Time Square on New Year's Eve.
sentences.zh: 除夕夜的时代广场。

sentences.en: Place in which alcohol is served.
sentences.zh: 供应酒精的场所。

sentences.en: Places where alcohol is served.
sentences.zh: 供应酒精的地方。

sentences.en: And they pepper Clement with these ideas about, well, couldn't New York bar guns in all these sensitive places?
sentences.zh: 他们不断向克莱门特抛出这些想法，比如，纽约难道不能在所有这些敏感场所禁枪吗？

sentences.en: So, Mr. Chief Justice, I think probably the right way to look at those cases would be look at them case by case and say, OK.
sentences.zh: 所以，首席大法官先生，我认为看待这些案件的正确方式可能是逐案审理，然后说，好吧。

sentences.en: And he's quite reluctant to engage.
sentences.zh: 而且他非常不情愿参与讨论。

sentences.en: This is not the argument he wants to have.
sentences.zh: 这不是他想要进行的辩论。

sentences.en: Sensitive places include government buildings and schools.
sentences.zh: 敏感场所包括政府大楼和学校。

sentences.en: I think those you can probably tap into a pretty good tradition.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些地方或许可以追溯到某种相当好的传统。

sentences.en: He concedes that, yes, some sensitive places can be regulated.
sentences.zh: 他承认，是的，某些敏感场所是可以监管的。

sentences.en: You can bar guns in some places.
sentences.zh: 你可以在某些地方禁止携带枪支。

sentences.en: Restriction of access to the place is something that I think would be consistent with the way government buildings have worked and schools have worked.
sentences.zh: 我认为，限制进入这些场所的做法，与政府大楼和学校一直以来的运作方式是一致的。

sentences.en: He doesn't want to get into the particulars.
sentences.zh: 他不想陷入细节讨论。

sentences.en: He says those are decisions to be made in later cases.
sentences.zh: 他说这些决定留待以后的案件中再做。

sentences.en: But you see the conservative justices drawing a distinction.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看到保守派大法官们划出了一条界线。

sentences.en: They're not happy about regulating people.
sentences.zh: 他们对监管个人并不乐见。

sentences.en: But they seem open to the broad regulation of places.
sentences.zh: 但他们似乎对广泛的场所监管持开放态度。

sentences.en: And they seem to think that might be a kind of compromise.
sentences.zh: 而且他们似乎认为这可能是一种妥协。

sentences.en: Let people, as a general matter, have licenses to carry guns in public.
sentences.zh: 让人们在一般情况下，拥有在公共场合携带枪支的许可。

sentences.en: But really shrink down what we mean by in public.
sentences.zh: 但真正缩小我们对“在公共场合”的定义。

sentences.en: So basically what this New York law says is that people are allowed to have concealed guns for self-defense outside the home if they've passed some sort of test that proves that they're a special case.
sentences.zh: 所以，纽约这项法律基本上规定，如果人们通过了某种证明他们属于特殊情况的测试，那么他们被允许在家庭以外的地方携带隐蔽枪支用于自卫。

sentences.en: But what Clement is saying and what the conservatives seem to be on board with is that there could just be a rule against guns at Yankee Stadium, regardless of who you are.
sentences.zh: 但克莱门特所说的是，保守派似乎也赞同，即可以制定一条规则，禁止在洋基体育场携带枪支，无论你是谁。

sentences.en: So in other words, it shouldn't be a rule limiting people, a rule limiting individuals.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这不应该是一条限制人的规则，一条限制个人的规则。

sentences.en: It should be a rule limiting which places are allowed.
sentences.zh: 而应该是一条限制哪些场所被允许的规则。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And Clement says he's not asking for anything radical.
sentences.zh: 克莱门特说他并没有要求任何激进的东西。

sentences.en: 43 jurisdictions allow their citizens to have the same rights that my clients are looking for.
sentences.zh: 有43个司法管辖区允许其公民享有我的客户所寻求的同样权利。

sentences.en: He says 43 states already do it this way and generally issue licenses or don't even require licenses for people who want to carry guns in public.
sentences.zh: 他说已经有43个州是这样做的，通常会发放许可证，甚至对那些想在公共场合携带枪支的人不要求许可证。

sentences.en: And he says those 43 states include very large cities.
sentences.zh: 而且他说这43个州包括非常大的城市。

sentences.en: Those states include major urban areas.
sentences.zh: 这些州包括主要的城市地区。

sentences.en: Like Phoenix.
sentences.zh: 比如凤凰城。

sentences.en: Like Houston.
sentences.zh: 比如休斯顿。

sentences.en: Like Chicago.
sentences.zh: 比如芝加哥。

sentences.en: Like Chicago.
sentences.zh: 比如芝加哥。

sentences.en: I mean, most people think that Chicago is like the world's worst city with respect to gun violence, Mr. Clement.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，大多数人认为芝加哥是世界上枪支暴力最严重的城市，克莱门特先生。

sentences.en: And that last point causes Justice Kagan to jump in and say Chicago is maybe not the best example.
sentences.zh: 最后这一点让卡根大法官插话，说芝加哥可能不是最好的例子。

sentences.en: Perhaps not the best choice of cities for Clement.
sentences.zh: 对于克莱门特来说，这可能不是城市选择的最佳范例。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I think he probably regrets that particular example.
sentences.zh: 我想他可能后悔举那个特定的例子了。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，律师。

sentences.en: OK, so what is the other side's argument?
sentences.zh: 好的，那么另一方的论点是什么？

sentences.en: What's New York saying?
sentences.zh: 纽约方面怎么说？

sentences.en: General Underwood.
sentences.zh: 安德伍德总律师。

sentences.en: Mr. Chief Justice, and may it please the court, for centuries, English and American law have imposed limits on carrying firearms in public in the interest of public safety.
sentences.zh: 首席大法官先生，法官阁下，几个世纪以来，为了公共安全，英国和美国法律一直对在公共场合携带枪支施加限制。

sentences.en: So Barbara Underwood, New York's Solicitor General, says there's a long history of letting states regulate guns outside the home.
sentences.zh: 所以纽约州副总检察长芭芭拉·安德伍德说，长期以来，各州一直有权监管家庭以外的枪支。

sentences.en: And that history matters because the conservatives, as a general proposition, look to what the founding generation thought the Constitution meant,
sentences.zh: 这段历史很重要，因为保守派通常会考察开国一代认为宪法意味着什么，

sentences.en: what its original public meaning was.
sentences.zh: 考察其最初的公众含义是什么。

sentences.en: The history runs from the 14th century Statute of Northampton, which prohibited carrying arms in fairs and markets and other public gathering places.
sentences.zh: 这段历史可以追溯到14世纪的《北安普顿法令》，该法令禁止在集市、市场和其他公共聚集场所携带武器。

sentences.en: And there's lots of historical evidence, starting with the Statute of Northampton in 1328, which said you can't go armed to markets and fairs.
sentences.zh: 而且有大量的历史证据，从1328年的《北安普顿法令》开始，就规定不能携带武器去市场和集市。

sentences.en: To similar laws adopted by half of the American colonies and states in the founding period.
sentences.zh: 一直到建国时期一半的美国殖民地和州所采用的类似法律。

sentences.en: And through the colonial era and through the early states, in which there was indisputably substantial historical evidence that the colonies and states did regulate guns in public.
sentences.zh: 贯穿殖民时代和早期建国时期，无可争议地存在大量历史证据，表明殖民地和各州确实对公共场合的枪支进行了监管。

sentences.en: And Barbara Underwood says.
sentences.zh: 芭芭拉·安德伍德说。

sentences.en: New York is not an outlier in the extent to which the state restricts the ability to carry firearms in public.
sentences.zh: 纽约州在限制公共场合携带枪支的能力方面并非特例。

sentences.en: And it's not an outlier in asking a licensed applicant to show good cause for a carry license.
sentences.zh: 在要求持枪许可申请人证明有正当理由方面，它也不是特例。

sentences.en: That should be enough reason to let some states do it their way and other states do it their way, that we don't need a uniform rule for this.
sentences.zh: 这应该足以让一些州按自己的方式行事，而另一些州按自己的方式行事，我们不需要为此制定统一的规则。

sentences.en: So how do the justices respond to that argument?
sentences.zh: 那么大法官们是如何回应这一论点的呢？

sentences.en: Her argument doesn't seem to get a lot of traction with the conservatives,
sentences.zh: 她的论点似乎并没有在保守派中引起太多共鸣，

sentences.en: who view the history as contested and in one sense already settled by the Heller decision and something they're not eager to revisit.
sentences.zh: 他们认为这段历史是有争议的，在某种意义上已经被“海勒案”判决所解决，而且他们并不急于重新审视。

sentences.en: General Underwood, you seem to rely a bit on the density of the population.
sentences.zh: 安德伍德总律师，你似乎有点依赖人口密度。

sentences.en: What they are quite curious about is why New York State seems to be much more apt to grant you a license if you're in a rural area rather than in an urban area like New York City.
sentences.zh: 他们非常好奇的是，为什么纽约州似乎更倾向于给农村地区的人发放许可证，而不是像纽约市这样的城市地区。

sentences.en: Heller relied on the right to defense as a basis for its reading of the Second Amendment.
sentences.zh: “海勒案”将自卫权作为解读宪法第二修正案的基础。

sentences.en: I would think that arises in more populated areas.
sentences.zh: 我认为这在人口稠密的地区更为突出。

sentences.en: If you're out in the woods, it's pretty unlikely that you're going to run into someone who's going to rob you on the street.
sentences.zh: 如果你在树林里，你不太可能遇到会在街上抢劫你的人。

sentences.en: So, for instance, Chief Justice Roberts says that he's not sure you have a real need for a gun for self-defense in upstate New York.
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，罗伯茨首席大法官说，他不确定你在纽约州北部是否真的需要枪支来防身。

sentences.en: He says...
sentences.zh: 他说……

sentences.en: Well, how many muggings take place in the forest?
sentences.zh: 那么，森林里发生了多少起抢劫案？

sentences.en: How many muggings take place in the forest?
sentences.zh: 森林里发生了多少起抢劫案？

sentences.en: If we...
sentences.zh: 如果我们……

sentences.en: How many do you think?
sentences.zh: 你认为有多少起？

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: His suggestion being that the places that are dangerous where you might need a gun for self-defense are in urban areas or the subway late at night.
sentences.zh: 他的暗示是，那些危险的、你可能需要枪支自卫的地方是在城市地区，或者是深夜的地铁里。

sentences.en: Now, a counterargument might be that you're much more likely to have law enforcement presence in an urban place than a rural place.
sentences.zh: 现在，一个反驳的观点可能是，在城市地区比在农村地区更有可能有执法人员存在。

sentences.en: But it's also the case that there's a great deal of gun violence in urban centers.
sentences.zh: 但同样的情况是，城市中心也存在大量的枪支暴力。

sentences.en: So, the arguments kind of cut both ways.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些论点在某种程度上是双向的。

sentences.en: General, you know, one of the things that strikes me about this area...
sentences.zh: 总律师，你知道，关于这个领域，有一件事让我印象深刻……

sentences.en: And Justice Kagan, a liberal, says that...
sentences.zh: 自由派的卡根大法官说……

sentences.en: It's a hard thing to match with our notion of constitutional rights generally.
sentences.zh: 这很难与我们对宪法权利的一般概念相匹配。

sentences.en: I mean, that level of local flexibility...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那种地方层面的灵活性……

sentences.en: It would be odd to have a constitutional right kind of have different force depending on what part of the state you happen to live in.
sentences.zh: 如果一项宪法权利根据你恰好居住在州的哪个部分而具有不同的效力，那将是很奇怪的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, the justices are kind of poking holes in this idea of the law being applied differently based on population density.
sentences.zh: 所以，大法官们正在对这种基于人口密度而不同地适用法律的想法提出质疑。

sentences.en: So, how does Underwood respond to that?
sentences.zh: 那么，安德伍德是如何回应的呢？

sentences.en: If you go right to history and tradition, the history was to regulate most strenuously in densely populated places.
sentences.zh: 如果你直接追溯历史和传统，历史上的做法是在人口稠密的地方进行最严格的监管。

sentences.en: That's what fairs and markets are.
sentences.zh: 这就是集市和市场的作用。

sentences.en: Her larger point is that guns are different in big cities.
sentences.zh: 她更宏大的观点是，在大城市里，枪支的情况有所不同。

sentences.en: But we also have a rationale for that history, which is that where there is dense population, there is also the deterrent of lots of people.
sentences.zh: 但我们对这段历史也有一个理由，那就是人口稠密的地方，也有许多人作为威慑力量。

sentences.en: And there is the availability of law enforcement in...
sentences.zh: 而且还有执法部门的可用性……

sentences.en: You may have less need for self-defense because there's law enforcement and police officers and transit police available to defend you in the city.
sentences.zh: 你可能对自卫的需求较少，因为城市里有执法人员、警察和交通警察可以保护你。

sentences.en: And in areas where people are packed densely together, as the questioning displays, the risks of harm from people who are packed shoulder to shoulder, all having guns,
sentences.zh: 而在人们拥挤在一起的地区，正如质询所展示的那样，人们肩并肩地挤在一起，如果每个人都有枪，那么伤害的风险……

sentences.en: are much more acute than they are...
sentences.zh: 要比……严重得多。

sentences.en: And that having lots of guns around is itself a threat to public safety.
sentences.zh: 而且周围有大量的枪支本身就是对公共安全的威胁。

sentences.en: So, if I'm understanding you correctly, Underwood, the lawyer on the New York side, is saying that in a populous city with all these people cheek by jowl,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我理解得没错，纽约方面的律师安德伍德是在说，在一个人口稠密、人们摩肩接踵的城市里，

sentences.en: a gun is more of a threat than it is a protection.
sentences.zh: 枪支带来的威胁比保护作用更大。

sentences.en: And if you want to make the case that you need one, you better have a really good reason.
sentences.zh: 如果你想证明你需要一把枪，你最好有一个非常充分的理由。

sentences.en: That captures her point, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这抓住了她的观点，是的。

sentences.en: I'm not sure it persuaded most of the justices, but that's what she said.
sentences.zh: 我不确定这是否说服了大多数大法官，但这就是她所说的。

sentences.en: So, I want you to think about people like this, people who work late at night in Manhattan.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想让你考虑一下这样的人，那些在曼哈顿深夜工作的人。

sentences.en: Justice Alito, for instance, pressed her on this.
sentences.zh: 例如，阿利托大法官就此向她施压。

sentences.en: He asked about workers in Manhattan, say, who work late, a hospital orderly, a doorman, you know,
sentences.zh: 他问到了曼哈顿的工人，比如深夜工作的医院护工、门卫，你知道，

sentences.en: the people who clean office buildings and have long commutes home through dangerous areas, having gotten out of work late to the outer boroughs.
sentences.zh: 那些打扫办公大楼、深夜下班后还要长途跋涉穿过危险地区回到外围行政区的人。

sentences.en: And they apply for a license and they say, look, nobody has told, has said, I'm going to mug you next Thursday.
sentences.zh: 他们申请许可证时说，看，没有人告诉我，没有人说，下周四我要抢劫你。

sentences.en: However, there have been a lot of muggings in this area and I am scared to death.
sentences.zh: 然而，这个地区发生了很多抢劫案，我吓坏了。

sentences.en: He suggested that they may well have a reason to want to have and should have a gun for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 他暗示他们很可能有理由想要并且应该拥有一把枪用于自卫。

sentences.en: And he asked Barbara Underwood.
sentences.zh: 他问芭芭拉·安德伍德。

sentences.en: They do not get licenses.
sentences.zh: 他们拿不到许可证。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Is that a good enough reason?
sentences.zh: 这是一个足够好的理由吗？

sentences.en: Would they get a license?
sentences.zh: 他们能拿到许可证吗？

sentences.en: That is in general right, yes.
sentences.zh: 总的来说是这样，是的。

sentences.en: If there's nothing particular to them, that's right.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没有什么特殊情况，就是这样。

sentences.en: And she candidly said no.
sentences.zh: 她坦率地说没有。

sentences.en: And I have a feeling that that exchange resonated with the justices on the right side of the court who probably would have liked a different answer.
sentences.zh: 我有一种感觉，这次交流引起了法院右翼大法官们的共鸣，他们可能希望得到不同的答案。

sentences.en: Thank you, counsel.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，律师。

sentences.en: The case is submitted.
sentences.zh: 案件已提交。

sentences.en: The Honorable Court is now adjourned until Monday next at 10 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 本庭现在休庭，下周一上午10点再开庭。

sentences.en: So, Adam, I want to step back and think a little bit about what this all means and what it means for gun rights in America.
sentences.zh: 所以，亚当，我想退一步思考一下这一切意味着什么，以及这对美国的枪支权利意味着什么。

sentences.en: It feels like there's a kind of fundamental disagreement playing out here about how people see guns, right?
sentences.zh: 感觉这里存在一种根本性的分歧，关于人们如何看待枪支，对吧？

sentences.en: At a basic level, one side sees guns as protection and a critical individual right.
sentences.zh: 在基本层面上，一方将枪支视为保护手段和关键的个人权利。

sentences.en: And on the other side, guns are seen as a potential threat.
sentences.zh: 而另一方面，枪支被视为一种潜在的威胁。

sentences.en: And this side believes it's warranted to put limits on that right.
sentences.zh: 这一方认为对该权利进行限制是合理的。

sentences.en: Is that how you see this case?
sentences.zh: 你也是这样看待这个案件的吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I think this is one of a zillion examples of the way Americans are polarized across many, many issues and simply have a fundamental,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是美国人在许多许多问题上两极分化，并且在根本上存在不可调和的意见分歧的无数例子之一，

sentences.en: irreconcilable difference of opinion about whether a gun keeps you safe or is a danger to the community.
sentences.zh: 即枪支是让你安全还是对社区构成危险。

sentences.en: And, you know, the justices split along the lines of public opinion, as you would predict by the parties of the presidents who appointed them.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，大法官们的分歧与公众舆论的路线一致，正如你根据任命他们的总统所属的党派所能预测的那样。

sentences.en: And this is one of those many gaps that's really hard to overcome.
sentences.zh: 这是那些确实难以克服的众多鸿沟之一。

sentences.en: Justice Alito, for instance, said there are lots of guns in New York City already.
sentences.zh: 例如，阿利托大法官说纽约市已经有很多枪了。

sentences.en: It's just that they're illegal.
sentences.zh: 只是它们是非法的。

sentences.en: The bad guys have them.
sentences.zh: 坏人拥有它们。

sentences.en: Why shouldn't law-abiding citizens be able to have them?
sentences.zh: 为什么守法公民不能拥有它们呢？

sentences.en: Other justices on the left seemed terrified by the idea that major urban centers would be overrun by guns, whether licensed or not.
sentences.zh: 左翼的其他大法官似乎对大城市被枪支淹没的想法感到恐惧，无论是否获得许可。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So what's going to happen then?
sentences.zh: 那么接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: How are the justices going to rule on this?
sentences.zh: 大法官们将如何裁决此案？

sentences.en: I'm almost certain that the New York licensing law will get struck down.
sentences.zh: 我几乎可以肯定，纽约的许可法将被推翻。

sentences.en: How broadly they do that is an open question.
sentences.zh: 他们会推翻到什么程度是一个悬而未决的问题。

sentences.en: They could say, I suppose, that it's too strict, but you can require people to make some kind of showing that they're entitled to have a gun.
sentences.zh: 我想他们可能会说，它太严格了，但你可以要求人们证明他们有权拥有枪支。

sentences.en: I think more likely the court will just say something like, if you don't have a criminal record,
sentences.zh: 我认为法院更有可能只是说，如果你没有犯罪记录，

sentences.en: you're allowed to have a gun in public in seven or so states where you currently can't without showing a special reason.
sentences.zh: 你就在目前无法在没有特殊理由的情况下持枪的七个左右的州里，被允许在公共场合携带枪支。

sentences.en: And that would make the country uniform on this point.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，全国在这一点上就统一了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So if they strike down this New York law,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们推翻了纽约州的这项法律，

sentences.en: they'd be doing that because the majority of the justices think it's just unconstitutional to deny some people access to guns simply because they haven't made a good enough case for why they need them for self-defense.
sentences.zh: 那是因为多数大法官认为，仅仅因为人们没能充分证明自己为何需要持枪自卫，就剥夺他们的持枪权是违宪的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then there's the question about what they do about sensitive places, which are not directly implicated in the case.
sentences.zh: 接下来还有一个问题，就是他们会如何处理“敏感场所”，这些场所并未直接涉及本案。

sentences.en: It's not part of what the justices agreed to decide, but it was such a big part of the argument that you could imagine there would be a substantial aside,
sentences.zh: 虽然这不在大法官们同意裁决的范围内，但它在辩论中占了很大比重，你可以想象，判决书中可能会有相当大篇幅的附言，

sentences.en: as there was in the Heller case, about things that we're not talking about today, but which may well be within New York's right to do.
sentences.zh: 就像在“海勒案”中那样，谈及我们今天未讨论、但很可能属于纽约州有权管辖的事项。

sentences.en: So it may be that the music of the decision will include a lot about here are the kinds of places where you can bar guns from,
sentences.zh: 所以，判决书的基调可能包含大量关于“哪些地方可以禁止持枪”的内容，

sentences.en: and that may dampen the effect of the decision to some extent.
sentences.zh: 这可能会在一定程度上减弱该裁决的影响力。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that, Adam?
sentences.zh: 亚当，你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: I mean, it could send two simultaneous messages.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它可能会同时传达出两个信号。

sentences.en: One, that as a general matter, everyone should have a right to have a license, to have a gun, wherever they want to go.
sentences.zh: 第一，从总体上讲，每个人都应该有权获得许可，有权在任何想去的地方持枪。

sentences.en: But that wherever they want to go can be strictly limited by the state to exclude places where large numbers of people gather.
sentences.zh: 但“任何想去的地方”可以被州政府严格限制，排除掉人群聚集的场所。

sentences.en: And so in that sense, it would dampen the effect of the first part of the decision.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，这会减弱该裁决第一部分的影响。

sentences.en: It sounds like you're saying they'll strike down the New York law, but it will remain unsettled exactly how local governments figure out what constitutes a sensitive place,
sentences.zh: 听起来你是说，他们会推翻纽约州的法律，但对于地方政府如何界定什么是“敏感场所”，

sentences.en: what constitutes places where you cannot carry a gun.
sentences.zh: 什么是禁止持枪的场所，依然没有定论。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And at its broadest level, you know, I think the most conservative justices were afraid the answer would be, well, what about Manhattan is a sensitive place?
sentences.zh: 而且从最广泛的层面来看，我认为最保守的大法官们担心答案会是：那么，曼哈顿算不算敏感场所？

sentences.en: What about any place where large numbers of people gather, where there's a substantial law enforcement presence?
sentences.zh: 任何人群聚集、有大量执法人员在场的地方算不算？

sentences.en: So that may be the next battleground for Second Amendment rights.
sentences.zh: 所以这可能是宪法第二修正案权利的下一个战场。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: In another 10 years' time.
sentences.zh: 再过10年吧。

sentences.en: Every 10 years or so, we've got a good Second Amendment case here.
sentences.zh: 大约每10年，我们就会遇到一个重要的第二修正案案件。

sentences.en: I mean, if you're right, Adam, this would be very momentous.
sentences.zh: 亚当，如果你说得对，那将是非常重大的。

sentences.en: I mean, it'd mean a huge expansion of gun rights in America, where states like New York would no longer really be able to have stricter gun laws than the rest of the country.
sentences.zh: 这意味着美国的持枪权将大幅扩张，像纽约州这样的州，将无法再制定比全国其他地区更严格的枪支法。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: The Heller decision was a big deal, but in some ways symbolic.
sentences.zh: “海勒案”的裁决意义重大，但在某种程度上具有象征意义。

sentences.en: The right to have a gun inside the home is much less controversial than the right to have guns everywhere.
sentences.zh: 在家中拥有枪支的权利，远没有在任何地方都能持枪的权利那样具有争议性。

sentences.en: And this is a looks like it's going to be a two step triumph for gun rights groups,
sentences.zh: 这看起来将是枪支权利团体取得的第二步胜利，

sentences.en: which got the court to endorse an individual right to own guns in a setting that doesn't particularly bother many people,
sentences.zh: 他们让法院认可了在某种特定环境下拥有枪支的个人权利，而这种环境并不会让许多人感到困扰，

sentences.en: that you should have a gun in your home to defend yourself.
sentences.zh: 那就是你应该在家里拥有一把枪来保护自己。

sentences.en: But many of those same people would have a different answer if you ask the question of, do they want people carrying guns everywhere?
sentences.zh: 但如果问他们是否希望人们到处都带着枪，许多人会有不同的答案。

sentences.en: So this second step of the Second Amendment litigation move is really enormous.
sentences.zh: 所以，第二修正案诉讼的这一第二步意义极其重大。

sentences.en: And again, if I'm right, it will move what was a symbolic decision in 2008 into a very consequential and practical one come June when most big Supreme Court decisions land.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，如果我没猜错，它将把2008年那项具有象征意义的裁决，转变为六月份最高法院发布大多数重大裁决时，一项极具影响力和实践意义的裁决。

sentences.en: Essentially, this question of whether one can have a right for self-defense has lived inside the home, been affirmed inside the home,
sentences.zh: 本质上，关于一个人是否拥有自卫权的这个问题，一直局限在家庭内部，并在家庭内部得到了确认，

sentences.en: and has now opened up the door and walked outside into the world.
sentences.zh: 而现在，它已经推开门，走到了外面的世界。

sentences.en: Yes, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Adam, thank you.
sentences.zh: 亚当，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sabrina.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨布丽娜。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: On this vote, the yeas are 228 and the nays are 206.
sentences.zh: 本次投票结果为赞成228票，反对206票。

sentences.en: The motion is adopted.
sentences.zh: 动议获得通过。

sentences.en: After months of negotiations and delays, the House of Representatives has passed a $1 trillion infrastructure bill,
sentences.zh: 经过数月的谈判和拖延，众议院通过了一项1万亿美元的基础设施法案，

sentences.en: the final step in delivering a key part of President Biden's economic agenda.
sentences.zh: 这是落实拜登总统经济议程关键部分的一步。

sentences.en: The bill, the largest investment in infrastructure in a decade, will finance roads, bridges, railroads and highways, internet access, improvements to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 该法案是十年来对基础设施最大规模的投资，将为道路、桥梁、铁路、高速公路、互联网接入、美国电网的改善，

sentences.en: power grid, and the protection of communities against climate change.
sentences.zh: 以及社区应对气候变化的保护措施提供资金。

sentences.en: Passage was uncertain until the very last moment on Friday.
sentences.zh: 直到周五最后一刻，法案能否通过仍不确定。

sentences.en: In the end, 13 House Republicans defied their leadership by voting for the bill, and six House Democrats defied their leadership by voting against it.
sentences.zh: 最终，13名共和党众议员违背党内领导层投票支持该法案，而6名民主党众议员则违背领导层投票反对。

sentences.en: Finally, infrastructure week.
sentences.zh: 终于，基础设施周来了。

sentences.en: I'm so happy to say that, infrastructure week.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能说出这句话，基础设施周。

sentences.en: After the vote, President Biden celebrated the bill's passage in a speech from the White House, saying it showed skeptical Americans that government can still work.
sentences.zh: 投票结束后，拜登总统在白宫发表讲话，庆祝法案通过，称这向持怀疑态度的美国人证明了政府依然可以有所作为。

sentences.en: Today's episode was produced by Lindsay Garrison, Robert Jimmison, Claire Tennesketter, and Daniel Guimet.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由琳赛·加里森、罗伯特·吉米森、克莱尔·坦内斯凯特和丹尼尔·吉梅特制作。

sentences.en: It was edited by Paige Cowett, engineered by Chris Wood, and features original music by Dan Powell.
sentences.zh: 由佩奇·考维特剪辑，克里斯·伍德担任音频工程师，原创音乐由丹·鲍威尔创作。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Jim Brumberg and Ben Landsverk of Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 主题音乐由Wonderly的吉姆·布鲁姆伯格和本·兰兹维克创作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Sabrina Tavernisi.
sentences.zh: 我是萨布丽娜·塔弗尼西。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》节目，我们将为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 敬请收听，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们会不会睡到不省人事。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们对光线有什么要求？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个非常具体的问题。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 你可以在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何播客平台上找到《Wirecutter秀》。
